# End to end, and the operational checklist {#sec-case-study} The package's two stages, run once, on one simulated dataset: `stage1_simulate()` builds the three-object contract of @sec-simulating-crosses, and `stage2_select()` selects hybrids from it under a grid of diversity budgets. That is the hybrid-selection side of a programme only. The stages S1 to S3 of @sec-stages (pool conservation, doubled-haploid (DH) crosses, line selection) and the crossing and testing design of @sec-mating, @sec-sparse and @sec-joint are not run here. Then the checklist, which draws on the whole book. ## The two stages in one script ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} st1 <- stage1_simulate(book_cfg) c(hybrids = nrow(st1$X), markers = ncol(st1$X), f_min = min(st1$f), f_max = max(st1$f)) #> hybrids markers f_min f_max #> 625.00000 2000.00000 0.64475 0.83175 ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} n_sel <- round(0.10 * nrow(st1$X)) res <- withCallingHandlers(stage2_select( X = st1$X, f = st1$f, hybrids = st1$hybrids, n_sel = n_sel, alphas = NULL, # NULL = automatic grid, 0 to the attainable ceiling weights = NULL, # NULL = equal weight across traits fL = st1$fL, # optional: enables theta_A / theta_B / theta_AB B_null = 500, B_full = 80, NP = 100, itermax = 200, verbose = FALSE), # muffle only DEoptim's advice that NP be >= 10 x the number of parameters warning = function(w) if (grepl("'NP'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")) ``` ::: The run's settings, which every number below depends on. It selects $n$ = 62 hybrids, 10 % of the $N$ = 625 candidates, where @sec-ocs, @sec-choosing and @sec-cycles select 60. The random-subset reference `gd_ref` comes from `B_null` = 500 subsets and the z-scores below from `B_full` = 80. The differential evolution (DE) runs with `NP` = 100 and `itermax` = 200, a nominal $2 \times 10^4$ evaluations per budget, against $6 \times 10^5$ at the package defaults (`NP` = 300, `itermax` = 2000). Every scenario is one run, with `seed = 1` for both the null and the DE; @sec-case-study-frontier repeats the call over further seeds and at the default DE budget, from a cache. The ceiling and the frontier below are therefore not comparable number for number with those of @sec-ocs or @sec-choosing, which use other $n$ and other $B$. ::: {.callout-note} ## The same functions as a script This chapter runs at the book's teaching scale (25 + 25 lines, 2000 markers). `inst/scripts/run_all.R` calls the same two functions at the `sim_config` default (50 + 50 lines, 5000 markers), which is not the package's declared production scale of 71 + 71 lines and 25000 markers (A8 of @sec-era-programme). It also uses other settings: $n$ at 4 % of the candidates, and the package defaults of `B_null`, `B_full`, `NP` and `itermax`. Its tables go to `report/`. `run_benchmark.R` produces the numbers quoted in `README.md`. Neither script is run by this chapter, and their run times are not measured here. ```sh Rscript inst/scripts/run_all.R Rscript inst/scripts/run_benchmark.R ``` ::: With real data only the first line changes: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} st1 <- stage1_build(X = my_hybrid_matrix, ped = my_pedigree, traits = my_predicted_traits, fL = my_line_coancestry) ``` ::: ### The reference values ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} unlist(res$ref) #> gd_ref gd_se alpha_max n_sel population_bias #> 3.259845e-01 3.556567e-05 3.938109e-02 6.200000e+01 6.467346e-03 # the ceiling is the achieved loss of the truncation plan stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal( res$metrics$alpha[res$metrics$scenario == "ref_truncation"], res$ref$alpha_max))) ``` ::: `alpha_max` in `res$ref` is the code name of the attainable ceiling $\alpha_{\text{trunc}}$ of @sec-ocs: the loss that pure truncation incurs, measured against the same-size baseline of @sec-baseline. It is not the budget $\alpha_{\max}$, which in this chapter, as in @sec-ocs, is the policy value a scenario requests. A requested budget at or above $\alpha_{\text{trunc}}$ constrains nothing. For a budget above it `stage2_select()` raises a warning that the constraint is inoperative, and then still runs the DE for that scenario and returns its plan under the `DE_alpha_*` label like any other. The automatic grid (`alphas = NULL`) ends at $\alpha_{\text{trunc}}$, so no such warning arises in this run. The call above muffles one warning only: the `DEoptim` advice that `NP` be at least ten times the number of parameters, which is raised once per DE run, 5 times in this call. Every other warning, the inoperative-budget one included, would surface. ### Metrics per scenario @tbl-case-study-metrics gives the metrics of the nine scenarios of this run. ::: {#tbl-case-study-metrics .cell layout-align="center" tbl-cap='Metrics of the selected set for each scenario of this run, as returned in `$metrics` by `stage2_select()` (the metrics are defined in @sec-catalogue). Five DE rows, one per requested budget, the name carrying $\alpha_{\max}$ in percent; four reference selections (`ref_*`). `alpha` is the achieved gene diversity loss against the same-size random baseline (a fraction); `index` is the mean index of the selected hybrids in standard deviations. Teaching scale (25 + 25 lines, 2000 markers), $n$ = 62 of $N$ = 625 candidates, DE and null seed 1.'} ```{.r .cell-code} fmt(res$metrics[, c("scenario", "alpha", "index", "Ns", "Ne_parents", "Ne_lines_A", "Ne_lines_B", "max_line", "alleles_lost")], 4) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|scenario | alpha| index| Ns| Ne_parents| Ne_lines_A| Ne_lines_B| max_line| alleles_lost| |:--------------|-------:|------:|------:|----------:|----------:|----------:|--------:|------------:| |DE_alpha_0.00 | 0.0000| 1.1004| 0.7418| 27.4571| 12.4805| 15.2540| 10| 63| |DE_alpha_0.98 | 0.0098| 1.4141| 0.7383| 22.3488| 9.1962| 14.2370| 14| 81| |DE_alpha_1.97 | 0.0195| 1.6767| 0.7349| 18.0894| 7.3359| 11.7914| 16| 106| |DE_alpha_2.95 | 0.0295| 1.8523| 0.7314| 15.8843| 5.9505| 11.9379| 20| 116| |DE_alpha_3.94 | 0.0357| 1.9600| 0.7292| 14.3701| 5.2948| 11.1744| 21| 125| |ref_truncation | 0.0394| 1.9701| 0.7280| 13.4877| 4.6878| 12.0125| 23| 124| |ref_trunc_cap | 0.0028| 0.7769| 0.7408| 31.6379| 15.7541| 15.8843| 4| 47| |ref_max_div | -0.0131| 0.1100| 0.7465| 36.9615| 18.6602| 18.3048| 5| 36| |ref_random | 0.0011| 0.0682| 0.7414| 37.3204| 17.9626| 19.4141| 6| 31|
::: ::: Read the `index` column against `alpha`. The scenario name carries the *requested* budget in percent (`DE_alpha_3.94` requests $\alpha_{\max} = \alpha_{\text{trunc}}$); the `alpha` column is the loss the plan *achieved*. The five `DE_` rows are the index each budget bought, on this dataset, at this selection intensity and at the evaluation budget stated above; @sec-case-study-frontier reads them as a frontier and states what limits that reading. The four `ref_` rows are reference selections, not budgets. Now read `Ne_parents` against `Ns` in the same rows. @sec-genomic-era calls for $F_{hom}$ and $F_{drift}$ to be computed separately (@sec-case-study-lenses does), and names `ne_parents()` as this book's implementation of the parent-count side of that diagnostic. `stage2_select()` has no argument that bounds `Ne_parents`, so in this run it is a report line, not a constraint (@tbl-case-study-ns): ::: {#tbl-case-study-ns .cell layout-align="center" tbl-cap='$N_s$ (`Ns`) and `Ne_parents` for each scenario of @tbl-case-study-metrics, and each divided by its maximum over the nine scenarios (`Ns_relative`, `Ne_par_relative`).'} ```{.r .cell-code} d <- res$metrics fmt(data.frame(scenario = d$scenario, Ns = d$Ns, Ne_parents = d$Ne_parents, Ns_relative = d$Ns / max(d$Ns), Ne_par_relative = d$Ne_parents / max(d$Ne_parents)), 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|scenario | Ns| Ne_parents| Ns_relative| Ne_par_relative| |:--------------|-----:|----------:|-----------:|---------------:| |DE_alpha_0.00 | 0.742| 27.457| 0.994| 0.736| |DE_alpha_0.98 | 0.738| 22.349| 0.989| 0.599| |DE_alpha_1.97 | 0.735| 18.089| 0.984| 0.485| |DE_alpha_2.95 | 0.731| 15.884| 0.980| 0.426| |DE_alpha_3.94 | 0.729| 14.370| 0.977| 0.385| |ref_truncation | 0.728| 13.488| 0.975| 0.361| |ref_trunc_cap | 0.741| 31.638| 0.992| 0.848| |ref_max_div | 0.747| 36.962| 1.000| 0.990| |ref_random | 0.741| 37.320| 0.993| 1.000|
::: ```{.r .cell-code} # GD = 1 - theta, Ns = 1/(2 theta), hence Ns is a function of the achieved alpha stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(d$GD, 1 - d$theta)), isTRUE(all.equal(d$Ns, 1 / (2 * d$theta))), isTRUE(all.equal(d$Ns, 1 / (2 * (1 - res$ref$gd_ref * (1 - d$alpha)))))) ``` ::: Result. $N_s$ goes from 0.7418 at $\alpha_{\max} = 0$ to 0.728 under truncation; `Ne_parents` goes from 27.5 to 13.5, against 37.3 for the random subset. The two columns are not on one scale. On molecular $\mathbf f$, $N_s = 1/(2\theta_S)$ lies in $[1/2, 1]$ at biallelic loci and is not a number of individuals (@sec-ns), so its ratio to its own maximum (`Ns_relative`) says nothing about the size of a pool. In this run $N_s$ is also fixed by the achieved loss: with gene diversity $GD_S = 1 - \theta_S$ and $\alpha = (GD_{\text{ref}} - GD_S)/GD_{\text{ref}}$ (@eq-catalogue-alpha), $N_s = 1/\{2[1 - GD_{\text{ref}}(1 - \alpha)]\}$ (all three asserted in the code of @tbl-case-study-ns), so the `Ns` column restates the constraint and adds nothing to the `alpha` column. Interpretation, and what limits it. The contrast that carries information is between the lens the budget pins ($\theta_S$, $GD_S$, $\alpha$, and therefore $N_s$) and a parent-count quantity it does not pin. A report limited to the first would not show the fall of `Ne_parents`. This is one dataset; the dispersion of `Ne_parents` over the optimiser's seed is given in @sec-case-study-frontier. ### Both lenses, and the pool partition {#sec-case-study-lenses} @tbl-case-study-lenses gives both lenses and the pool partition for each scenario. ::: {#tbl-case-study-lenses .cell layout-align="center" tbl-cap='The two lenses and the pool partition for each scenario of @tbl-case-study-metrics: achieved loss `alpha` (a fraction), `F_hom` and `F_drift` on the frozen base $p_0$, their gap `cov_diag`, `rare_retained` (the fraction of the candidate pool\'s rare alleles still present in the selected set), the within-hybrid gene diversity `GD_WI_hyb`, the between-pool component `GD_BS` and the statistic `F_ST` $= GD_{BS}/GD_T$.'} ```{.r .cell-code} fmt(res$metrics[, c("scenario", "alpha", "F_hom", "F_drift", "cov_diag", "rare_retained", "GD_WI_hyb", "GD_BS", "F_ST")], 4) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|scenario | alpha| F_hom| F_drift| cov_diag| rare_retained| GD_WI_hyb| GD_BS| F_ST| |:--------------|-------:|-------:|-------:|--------:|-------------:|---------:|------:|------:| |DE_alpha_0.00 | 0.0000| 0.0038| 0.0161| -0.0123| 0.8636| 0.1834| 0.0393| 0.1205| |DE_alpha_0.98 | 0.0098| 0.0132| 0.0248| -0.0116| 0.8312| 0.1829| 0.0417| 0.1293| |DE_alpha_1.97 | 0.0195| 0.0224| 0.0348| -0.0124| 0.7727| 0.1828| 0.0452| 0.1414| |DE_alpha_2.95 | 0.0295| 0.0352| 0.0422| -0.0069| 0.7143| 0.1818| 0.0471| 0.1490| |DE_alpha_3.94 | 0.0357| 0.0377| 0.0490| -0.0113| 0.7143| 0.1821| 0.0499| 0.1586| |ref_truncation | 0.0394| 0.0412| 0.0534| -0.0121| 0.7338| 0.1822| 0.0514| 0.1640| |ref_trunc_cap | 0.0028| 0.0154| 0.0114| 0.0039| 0.7273| 0.1816| 0.0370| 0.1138| |ref_max_div | -0.0131| -0.0124| 0.0063| -0.0187| 0.9481| 0.1853| 0.0362| 0.1096| |ref_random | 0.0011| 0.0081| 0.0066| 0.0015| 0.9481| 0.1805| 0.0357| 0.1097|
::: ::: `F_ST` is the statistic $GD_{BS}/GD_T$ of @eq-f-stats computed on each selected set. It is not the Balding-Nichols parameter $F_{BN}$ of the simulation. `alpha` constrains the first lens only. `F_drift` is the lens it does not pin, and `cov_diag` is exactly the gap between them, $F_{hom} - F_{drift}$ (@eq-era-cov; Eq. 3 of @meuwissen2020). The largest absolute deviation over the nine rows is printed below and asserted to lie within 100 machine epsilons, the tolerance of an exact identity; the package's test suite asserts it too (`tests/testthat/test-lenses.R`): ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} dev_eq3 <- max(abs(d$cov_diag - (d$F_hom - d$F_drift))) stopifnot(dev_eq3 < 100 * .Machine$double.eps) c(max_deviation_from_Eq3 = dev_eq3) #> max_deviation_from_Eq3 #> 6.678685e-17 ``` ::: Result. `GD_BS` rises with the budget, from 0.0393 at $\alpha_{\max} = 0$ to 0.0514 under truncation, against 0.0357 for the random subset. Its cause is not identified here: concentrating the use of a few lines inside a pool raises $GD_{BS}$ with no change in the lines (@tbl-catalogue-gdbs-conc), and this run has no arm that separates that effect from selection. The index is additive and the model has no dominance (@sec-case-study-limits), so the rise is not evidence about heterosis; $GD_{BS}$ stands for the divergence heterosis rests on only under the conditions of @tbl-keystone (flat dominance, inbred parents, a complete factorial). @sec-stages is the reason to watch it rather than celebrate it. ### Distance from the random null @tbl-case-study-z places six of the metrics against the random null. ::: {#tbl-case-study-z .cell layout-align="center" tbl-cap='Six metrics for each scenario of @tbl-case-study-metrics, in standard deviations from the random-subset null (`B_full` = 80 random subsets of the same size). Less diverse than chance is negative for `z_GD`, `z_Ne_parents` and `z_rare_retained`, and positive for `z_F_drift` and `z_ANE`; `z_GD_BS` has no worse direction.'} ```{.r .cell-code} fmt(res$z_scores[, c("scenario", "z_GD", "z_Ne_parents", "z_F_drift", "z_rare_retained", "z_GD_BS", "z_ANE")], 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|scenario | z_GD| z_Ne_parents| z_F_drift| z_rare_retained| z_GD_BS| z_ANE| |:--------------|------:|------------:|---------:|---------------:|-------:|-----:| |DE_alpha_0.00 | 0.00| -5.63| 7.71| -4.27| 6.57| 6.96| |DE_alpha_0.98 | -5.20| -8.56| 14.78| -5.69| 11.05| 9.97| |DE_alpha_1.97 | -10.35| -11.00| 22.79| -8.24| 17.33| 19.86| |DE_alpha_2.95 | -15.63| -12.26| 28.76| -10.80| 20.87| 17.76| |DE_alpha_3.94 | -18.88| -13.13| 34.27| -10.80| 25.81| 16.12| |ref_truncation | -20.85| -13.64| 37.81| -9.94| 28.51| 9.80| |ref_trunc_cap | -1.47| -3.23| 3.95| -10.23| 2.44| 17.27| |ref_max_div | 6.91| -0.18| -0.16| -0.57| 0.96| 5.91| |ref_random | -0.59| 0.03| 0.08| -0.57| 0.12| -0.43|
::: ::: Every metric in standard deviations from random selections of the same size (`B_full` = 80 subsets). The direction of "less diverse than chance" differs by column: negative for `z_GD`, `z_Ne_parents` and `z_rare_retained`, positive for `z_F_drift` and `z_ANE`. `ANE` is A-NE (accession-to-nearest-entry), the mean distance from each candidate to its nearest selected hybrid (@eq-catalogue-ene-ane), where lower means better representation. `z_GD_BS` has no "worse" direction. A z near zero says that a metric does not separate the plan from chance. It does not say that the metric is not acting as a constraint. `z_GD` is 0 at `DE_alpha_0.00`, the scenario in which $GD$ is the binding constraint, and it is near zero on average only. That scenario holds $\alpha$ at 0, so its $GD$ sits at `gd_ref`, the mean of the `B_null` = 500 draws; `z_GD` is centred and scaled on the separate `B_full` = 80 draws. The difference between the two Monte Carlo means gives `z_GD` at $\alpha = 0$ a standard deviation of about $\sqrt{1/80 + 1/500}$ = 0.12 z units (independent draws, and the `B_full` standard deviation taken as exact); the value printed at this seed is one draw of that error. A constrained metric is read against its budget. The metrics the constraint does not pin are the ones that move under it: at the same scenario `z_Ne_parents` is -5.6 and `z_F_drift` is 7.7. Each z divides by a standard deviation estimated from 80 subsets; if the null is close to normal, which is not checked here, that standard deviation carries a relative standard error of $1/\sqrt{2(B_{full} - 1)}$ = 8 % (@sec-catalogue-null), not shown in @tbl-case-study-z. ### The selection table @tbl-case-study-selection shows the hybrids selected under the most scenarios. ::: {#tbl-case-study-selection .cell layout-align="center" tbl-cap='The first eight rows of the selection table `$selection`, ordered by `n_scenarios`: each hybrid with its two parent lines, 1 in a scenario\'s column if that scenario selects it and 0 otherwise, and `n_scenarios`, the number of the nine scenarios of @tbl-case-study-metrics that select it.'} ```{.r .cell-code} scn <-setdiff(names(res$selection), c(names(st1$hybrids), "n_scenarios")) head(res$selection[order(-res$selection$n_scenarios), c("hybrid", "line_A", "line_B", scn, "n_scenarios")], 8) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}

::: ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} de_cols <- grep("^DE_", scn, value = TRUE) c(scenarios = length(scn), chosen_in_all_DE = sum(rowSums(res$selection[, de_cols, drop = FALSE]) == length(de_cols)), never_chosen = sum(res$selection$n_scenarios == 0), total_candidates = nrow(res$selection)) #> scenarios chosen_in_all_DE never_chosen total_candidates #> 9 18 386 625 ``` ::: `n_scenarios` counts, for each hybrid, the scenarios that select it, the four reference rows included. `chosen_in_all_DE` counts the hybrids selected under all five DE budgets of this run (DE and null seed 1). Whether the same hybrids recur under another seed of the optimiser is read from the same call repeated over DE/null seeds at the chapter's DE budget and at the package default, cached by `regenerate.R case_study` (seed 1 at the chapter budget is asserted to be this run): ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} kept <- read.csv(book_data("case_study_kept.csv")) live_kept <- res$selection$hybrid[ rowSums(res$selection[, de_cols, drop = FALSE]) == length(de_cols)] stopifnot(setequal(kept$hybrid[kept$budget == "chapter" & kept$seed == 1], live_kept)) kept_seeds <- sort(unique(kept$seed)) kept_tab <- t(vapply(c("chapter", "default"), function(b) { s <- split(kept$hybrid[kept$budget == b], factor(kept$seed[kept$budget == b], levels = kept_seeds)) c(seeds = length(s), min_kept = min(lengths(s)), max_kept = max(lengths(s)), kept_in_every_seed = length(Reduce(intersect, s)), kept_in_any_seed = length(Reduce(union, s))) }, numeric(5))) kept_tab #> seeds min_kept max_kept kept_in_every_seed kept_in_any_seed #> chapter 10 15 23 1 41 #> default 10 8 24 0 45 ``` ::: Over 10 seeds, the number of hybrids kept under every DE budget ranges from 15 to 23 at the chapter's DE budget and from 8 to 24 at the default. The sets do not coincide: the number kept under every budget in all 10 seeds is 1 at the chapter budget and 0 at the default, out of 41 and 45 kept in at least one seed. Within a run the plan keeps a core across budgets; which hybrids form it depends on the optimiser's seed, so no set of hybrids is shown here to be robust to the choice of $\alpha$. ## Reading the frontier {#sec-case-study-frontier} @fig-case-study-frontier draws the five DE rows of this run as a line and the four reference rows as separate marks. Behind them is the same `stage2_select()` call repeated over DE/null seeds at the chapter's DE budget and at the package default, cached by `regenerate.R case_study`. `seed` drives both the null and the DE, so the two budgets are paired by seed; seed 1 at the chapter budget is asserted to reproduce this run. `k` is the position in the automatic grid, because the requested $\alpha_{\max}$ moves with `gd_ref` and hence with the seed. @tbl-case-study-frontier gives the mean and standard deviation of the index over seeds at each budget, and the paired gain of the default budget with its standard error and the number of seeds in which it is positive: ::: {#tbl-case-study-frontier .cell layout-align="center" tbl-cap='The DE frontier over DE/null seeds, by grid point `k` (position in the automatic grid). `alpha_req_pct`: mean requested budget $\alpha_{\max}$ (%). `index_ch`, `sd_ch`: mean and standard deviation of the index over seeds at the chapter\'s DE budget (`NP` = 100, `itermax` = 200). `index_def`, `sd_def`: the same at the package default (`NP` = 300, `itermax` = 2000). `gain`: mean paired gain of the default budget over the chapter budget, seed by seed; `se_gain`: its standard error; `gain_pos`: the number of seeds in which it is positive. Index in standard deviations. Between successive DE budgets the index rises by 0.32, 0.27, 0.18, 0.18 index units per percentage point of achieved $\alpha$, from the tightest budget to the loosest. At the loosest budget the DE plan scores 1.96 at $\alpha$ = 0.0357; the truncation plan scores 1.97 at $\alpha$ = 0.0394, a loss that budget allows. The warm start of `stage2_select()` (greedy plans and the capped truncation) does not include the truncation plan. Over the 10 seeds, the standard deviation of the index at the chapter budget is between 0.001 and 0.023 across the five grid points. The default budget raises the index at the four tighter points by 0.063, 0.042, 0.034, 0.04 (standard errors at most 0.008), and at the loosest by 0.001 (s.e. 0.001, positive in 7 of 10 seeds). Truncation scores above the DE at the loosest budget in 10 of 10 seeds at the chapter budget and in 10 at the default, by 0.0057 to 0.0102 index units over the 20 (seed, budget) pairs. Secant slopes of the default-budget means are 0.32, 0.23, 0.16, 0.12 index units per percentage point. `Ne_parents` at $\alpha_{\max} = 0$ ranges from 25.3 to 27.5 over the seeds at the chapter budget. Interpretation, and what limits it. The DE curve is a price list of this run, not the constrained optimum. At the chapter's evaluation budget part of each price is the optimiser's shortfall: the default budget moves the tighter points by more than their seed-to-seed spread. Its loosest point stays below a feasible plan at both budgets run, so that shortfall is not closed by the 30-fold increase in nominal evaluations ($\texttt{NP} \times \texttt{itermax}$) between them; no larger budget was run. The warm start lacks the truncation plan; whether adding it closes the gap is not run here. How much of the default-budget price is still shortfall is not separated, because no bound (`ocs_bound()`, @sec-bound) is computed here, and all of it is one simulated dataset. The secant slopes show no sharp knee at either budget, and none is located. As in @sec-ocs, where along the frontier to set the budget is the programme's decision. Nor is the trade a permanent loss against a one-off gain: in @sec-cycles the index gain accumulates over cycles, and what the budgets leave for later cycles is that chapter's subject, not this one's. ## What this simulation cannot tell you {#sec-case-study-limits} Stated plainly, because the numbers above are precise and precision invites more confidence than the model supports. **The index carries no prediction error.** The traits are built from *known* marker effects (@sec-simulating-crosses). @sec-choosing (Finding 5) measures, within one cycle at the teaching scale, what happens when they are predicted: the plan's reported index is biased upward, and for truncation at nominal accuracy $r$ = 0.6, error correlated with relatedness costs more gene diversity than independent error of the same nominal accuracy. @sec-genomic-prediction fits the accuracies that validation schemes actually give. The reported `index` of a plan here should be read as an upper bound on what it would deliver in this one cycle; across cycles no such bound is claimed (@sec-cycles, C7). **The model is additive.** The index is a sum of additive marker effects. It misses heterosis and specific combining ability, which is precisely what a hybrid programme sells. The diversity constraint does not need a dominance model; the *mean-performance ranking* does (@sec-heterosis). Do not conflate them, and do not use these `index` values as performance predictions. **The pools are symmetric by construction, and still erode unevenly.** Both are drawn from the same ancestral frequencies at the same Balding-Nichols parameter, $F_{BN}$ = 0.15 (`fst` in `sim_config`, @eq-balding-nichols). Even so, truncation leaves `Ne_lines_A` = 4.69 and `Ne_lines_B` = 12.01 in @tbl-case-study-metrics. Because the two pools are exchangeable by construction, which of them erodes faster in a run is a property of that draw, not of pool A or B, and this chapter runs one draw. Per-pool reporting (`ne_lines_pool()`) is therefore needed even when the pools are alike. Real pools that differ in size, history and internal structure would add a systematic difference on top, which this simulation does not represent. **$N_s$ is not a drift projection.** It is a static descriptor of a set, in $[1/2, 1]$ on molecular $\mathbf f$ (@sec-ns). Do not extrapolate it forward. **What the run assumes and does not test.** The parent lines are fully inbred (A2 of @sec-era-programme). The markers are biallelic and drawn independently (no linkage), and they are also the loci of the index: `simulate_data()` gives every marker an effect on each trait (@sec-simulating-crosses), so the markers the metrics read are themselves under selection. Every one of the 25 x 25 crosses is made and evaluated, so the crossing plan and the testing design that would produce the 625 values (@sec-mating, @sec-sparse, @sec-joint) are assumed away. $n$ is 10 % of the candidates, no line has a usage cap (`max_use = NULL`), and the selector is the hybrid-key DE of `stage2_select()`, not the routes compared in @sec-advanced. Each of these is a choice of this run; none of the numbers above is shown to hold without it. **One cycle, not a trajectory.** Every result here is a single round of hybrid selection. @sec-stages found, in 8 cached founder pools of one external study, that a diversity term on cross choice at S2 lowered the S2 loss and raised the S3 and S4 losses, and could not say whether it changed the effective size of the final set (a set the file does not record) or the marker alleles retained; the gene diversity of the final set, the outcome that was higher with the term in most pools, was added post hoc. The same question applies across cycles. A one-cycle constraint is not a multi-cycle policy: @sec-cycles runs fifteen cycles from five founder draws, and on the mean over draws the unconstrained programme has the higher index in the early cycles and the $\alpha_{\max} = 0.02$ programme in the later ones; the crossing is not resolved by five draws (@sec-cycles-trajectory). **$p_0$ must be frozen.** `build_ctx()` sets $p_0$ to the column means of the `X` it is given, on every call. This chapter makes one call, so $p_0$ is the frequency over the 625 candidates. In a multi-cycle programme it must be the founder cycle's frequencies, held fixed (`run_cycles()` does so, @sec-cycles-freezing) -- the single most common error in applying `F_hom` and `F_drift` (@sec-genomic-era). @sec-cycles shows the failure directly: re-anchored each generation and read on the set the base was built from, five generations of real drift are reported as exactly none. ## The operational checklist ### Setting up - The base $p_0$ is frozen at the founding cycle and documented. - Diversity is computed on molecular coancestry `f`, never on a centred VanRaden `G`, whose elements sum to zero by construction (@eq-g-sum-zero, @sec-why-not-g). - The marker panel's minor allele frequency (MAF) spectrum is known -- it decides how severely the two lenses diverge. - Heterotic-group assignment is recorded, with the method that produced it, and treated as uncertain. ### Choosing the budget - The attainable ceiling $\alpha_{\text{trunc}}$ is computed *before* choosing $\alpha_{\max}$ (@sec-ocs). A budget at or above the ceiling constrains nothing. - Loss is measured against a **same-size resampling baseline**, never against the full pool (@sec-baseline). - The constraint is applied at the target set size, not incrementally. - The frontier is traced and the budget is set on it by the programme, rather than as a round number fixed in advance. Neither @sec-ocs nor this chapter finds a sharp knee to locate. ### Running the optimiser - The route and its evaluation budget are stated. `stage2_select()`, the route this chapter runs, is `sel_de()` on $n$ hybrid keys (@sec-combinatorial); the line-weight encoding is `sel_de_fast()`. No experiment in the book isolates the encoding, and the closest comparison favours `sel_de()` uncapped (@sec-advanced). - The differential evolution is **warm-started** from greedy solutions (@sec-combinatorial-warm). - If a per-line usage cap applies, the way it is enforced is stated: `sel_de()` adds it to the fitness as a penalty, and `sel_de_fast()` satisfies it in the decoder by construction (@sec-defast-restrictions). This chapter's run has no cap. - $N_{e,\text{par}}$ is a report line, read against the random null, unless the route accepts a floor on it. Among the package's routes only `sel_de_fast()` does, as a penalty that can bind but is not guaranteed met (@sec-defast-restrictions); the achieved $N_{e,\text{par}}$ is checked against the floor. In this chapter it is a report line. - The plan is checked against the Lagrangian bound `ocs_bound()` (@sec-bound), not against a point of the continuous relaxation inside the budget, which is not a bound. Its `converged` attribute, a stalling criterion rather than a certificate, is read first: converged and the gap small, the gap is the most further search can gain if that criterion is trusted; converged and the gap large, keep going; not converged, no gap is reported (@sec-advanced). A gap is the sum of the optimiser's shortfall and the relaxation's, and does not separate them (@sec-combinatorial). This chapter computes no bound and no gap. ### Validating the plan - `F_hom` and `F_drift` are computed **separately** and reported together, with `cov_diag` as the diagnostic, on a panel not used in the management where one exists (@sec-era-step5). - Allelic richness $A_{\text{ret}}$ (@sec-richness) is computed on the returned plan. It is not the only quantity $\theta$ leaves free: `F_drift` is another (@sec-case-study-lenses), and @sec-choosing (Finding 3) finds A-NE and E-NE (entry-to-nearest-entry) keeping as much rank variation at fixed $\theta$ as allelic richness does. This chapter reports $A_{\text{lost}}$ (`alleles_lost`) and `rare_retained`, not $A_{\text{ret}}$. - The within/between pool decomposition confirms diversity was not preserved by degrading pool separation. - The number of selected parent lines is biologically plausible. - $N_s$ is reported as a static descriptor in $[1/2, 1]$ (@sec-ns), not as a head count; a rate-based $N_e$ is **not** reported under active management (@sec-choosing-recommendation). - Every metric is reported against the random null, in standard deviations; a constrained metric is read against its budget, not against zero. ### Across cycles - The per-stage loss ledger of @sec-stages-ledger is kept (not the year-by-year diversity ledger of @sec-programme-ledger). In the one study the book has (8 cached founder pools), S2, DH induction, carries the largest share of the summed stage losses under cross selection on merit alone, and with a diversity term the three stages carry similar shares (@sec-stages); where diversity goes in general is not established. - The regression of $\log(1 - F)$ on cycle is checked for linearity (@sec-era-step4, @sec-cycles-rate). Curvature means a non-constant rate. The regression is read as that diagnostic and is not converted into a rate-based $N_e$; a high $R^2$ does not validate a projection from the fitted rate, and the covariance term is outside every one-locus metric (@sec-limits). - Periodic germplasm injection is planned. The evidence is one simulation reviewed in @sec-plant-literature [@sanchez2023], in which a closed elite pool depletes under a within-pool constraint, and @sec-cycles, in which all three closed budgets are still losing diversity at cycle 15 (five founder draws). Injection has a cost: there one injection of the programme's own founder lines raised $GD_T$ and lowered $F_{drift}$ and the index, and the index had not recovered by cycle 15. - The diversity cost per cycle is reported when cycle time is shortened. No chapter of this book measures it as a rate: @sec-programme reports the cost of shorter cycles as a 15-year stock because its cycles overlap, and @sec-cycles has discrete cycles of fixed length. ## Where to go next Three extensions the material here supports but does not cover, each needing new work rather than new derivation: **Real data ingestion.** `load_data()` is the single swap point and is currently a stub. A worked path from a variant call format (VCF) file to the `X`/`f`/`hybrids` contract is what most readers will need first, and it is the one extension here that is pure engineering rather than new derivation. **Estimating the dominance effects.** @sec-heterosis shows that expected heterosis depends on the alignment between divergence and $d$, and that no frequency-based statistic can see $d$. Ranking crosses on more than the mean needs the dominance effects locus by locus, which the book does not estimate. Setting the $\lambda$ of @sec-catalogue needs less: two covariances of $d$ with the frequencies, not $d$ itself (@sec-heterosis-lambda). @sec-heterosis-protocol sets out what a programme would run to obtain them. **Prediction error compounded across cycles.** @sec-choosing Finding 5 measures it within one cycle and @sec-cycles assumes it away (C7). The two have not been run together. Correlated error concentrates the selection (@sec-choosing), and in @sec-cycles the per-cycle gain is associated with the genic variance of the parents, an association that chapter does not test as a mechanism; how the two would combine across cycles is not known. ## Reproduce this chapter {.unnumbered} All the code of this chapter, in order and with the explanation kept as comments, is one script: [**12-case-study.R**](https://ederdbs.github.io/QG/downloads/12-case-study.R){download="12-case-study.R"}. Download it, install `hybdiv`, and run it top to bottom in an empty directory; cached results are fetched on first use.
